plants.name: Paeonia officinalis
plants.description: Plump, ruffled blooms open like silk pom-poms on sturdy stems above glossy, deeply cut leaves. The flowers are lavishly layered and often lightly fragrant. Each plant puts on a short, spectacular show of about a week or two, and bees and garden visitors both come for it.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (roughly May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Temperate gardens across Europe and North America, native to southern Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies are among the longest-lived garden perennials. A well-sited plant can bloom for decades, and some have been known to outlive the gardeners who planted them.

plants.name: Rhododendron ponticum
plants.description: Dense rounded clusters of bell-shaped, purple-mauve flowers, each speckled with tiny golden-green freckles, light up dark evergreen foliage. Whole woodland hillsides can glow violet as the flower trusses open.
plants.location: Woodlands and estates of the British Isles and western Europe, native to the Black Sea region and Iberia
plants.funFact: Introduced to Britain as an ornamental in the 1700s, this species spread so successfully that it is now considered invasive in many woodlands.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia
plants.description: Tall golden-lemon flower spikes, bristling with hundreds of tiny wiry blooms, rise from a rugged, silvery-leaved tree. In the Australian winter they glow against coastal dunes and offer a rich feast for nectar-feeding birds, bees and bats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Main flowering from January to June, with some plants blooming most of the year
plants.location: Eastern coastal Australia, from Queensland to Victoria
plants.funFact: Banksias are a vital winter food source for native wildlife, offering nectar when little else is in flower. Their woody seed cones later inspired the 'Banksia men' of Australian children's literature.
